questions.q: In medallion architecture, what characterizes the bronze layer?
options: Raw data, as extracted, untouched
Fully aggregated business metrics
Only data that has passed quality checks
Data that exists only inside Power BI
questions.explain: Bronze is the landing zone — raw data kept exactly as it arrived, before any cleaning or transformation.

questions.q: What is the key lineage difference between a view and a materialized table?
options: A view recomputes from source tables on every query, with no lag; a materialized table reflects its last refresh and can be stale
A view is always faster to query than a materialized table
A materialized table can never be traced for lineage
Views don't support column-level lineage, but materialized tables do
questions.explain: A view has no lineage lag — it reflects upstream changes instantly. A materialized table is frozen as of its last refresh, which may be stale.

questions.q: In the medallion pattern, what typically happens in the silver layer?
options: Deduplication, type standardization, and filtering/flagging of bad rows
Raw extraction directly from the source system
Final business aggregation for executive dashboards
Nothing — silver is a synonym for bronze
questions.explain: Silver is the cleaned, conformed layer — still roughly one row per source record, but now standardized and trustworthy.

questions.q: A data warehouse's dimensional model is typically organized around which two table types?
options: Fact tables and dimension tables
Bronze tables and gold tables only
Views and stored procedures only
Source tables and API tables
questions.explain: Fact tables hold events (sales, orders); dimension tables hold context (customers, products, dates) — together they form the dimensional model.

questions.q: Why does knowing whether a downstream object is a view or a materialized table matter for root-cause analysis?
options: It tells you whether a wrong number could still be in flight upstream, or is already frozen as of a past refresh
It determines which programming language was used to build it
It has no effect on lineage or troubleshooting
It only matters for choosing a chart type
questions.explain: A view always reflects the current upstream state; a materialized table reflects only its last refresh — knowing which you're looking at narrows down when a problem could have been introduced.
